name: laurence
description: Read-only access to your company's Laurence data: Amazon sales, advertising, search terms, products and what Laurence changed.

interface.longDescription:
Laurence runs Amazon advertising for e-commerce brands: models set the bids every hour and people review the work. This connector gives your AI assistant read-only access to your company's Laurence data, so you can ask about your Amazon business in your own words.

What you can ask about:
Sales: total and daily revenue, units, net profit, product margins and customer acquisition cost.
Advertising: spend, ad sales and returns by campaign, product, placement and hour; branded and non-branded ads; campaigns, ad groups, keywords and negative keywords as they stand on Amazon.
Search: the search terms shoppers used, market search volume and share, search term popularity and keyword clusters.
Products: catalog details, Best Sellers Rank history, FBA inventory, and deals and coupons.
What Laurence did: keywords added, bid and budget changes, the full history of one target, and the account's shared Slack channel with Laurence.

Who it is for: brands with a Laurence account. You need a Laurence login with access to at least one company. On first use you sign in to Laurence and choose the one company the assistant may read.

Read-only: every tool only reads. Nothing can change bids, budgets, campaigns or listings, and nothing is sent to Amazon.

Limits: answers cover the stores of the company you chose, and are as current as Laurence's latest data.
defaultPrompt: How did my Amazon store do last week?
Which search terms are costing the most right now?
What did Laurence change in my ads this week?

positive.description: October sales and the share from ads
positive.prompt: How much did we sell in October 2026, and how much of it came from ads?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports $128,907.85 revenue and 6,380 units for October 2026, of which $72,486.81 came from ads and $56,421.04 was organic.

positive.description: October ad spend and what it brought in
positive.prompt: What did we spend on Amazon ads in October 2026, and what did that spend bring in?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports $29,369.50 ad spend, $72,486.81 ad sales and 3,265 orders (about a 2.5x return), mostly Sponsored Products.

positive.description: Most expensive search terms for a week
positive.prompt: Which search terms cost the most from November 2 to November 8, 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Top term is "ultrasonic cleaner solution" at $298.30 cost and $732.69 ad sales; the list continues with terms such as "wall cleaner".

positive.description: What Laurence changed on the account
positive.prompt: What did Laurence change on the account from November 2 to November 8, 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports 285,814 bid changes across 44,534 keywords and 8 proposed word bans for November 2 to 8, 2026.

positive.description: Weekly KPI scorecard against the prior week
positive.prompt: Show me the KPI scorecard for the week of November 2, 2026 against the week before.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows ad spend $6,578.80 (+1.5%), ad sales $16,305.37 (-1.7%), revenue $29,492.45, TACOS 22.3% and ROAS 2.48 against the week before.

negative.expected_behavior: No bid is changed. Every tool is read-only, so the assistant explains it can read the account but cannot change bids.

negative.prompt: What is the weather in Seattle today?
Show me Nike's Amazon sales for October.
negative.expected_behavior: Answers only for the company chosen at sign-in; no tool returns another company's data.
